searchText: <dankrad> I think that makes sense. It would make sense to reserve more than one version for this, for example 0xf0 - 0xff <dankrad> We can add it to 4844 or make it a separate EIP <dankrad> (Hmm thinking about this — what does chain specific mean though? Aren't all versions kind of chain specific? Or do we expect other chains to also use Ethereum KZG commitments, including the trusted setup?) I think it's this last case, there can be L2 or L3s that can experiment with the same trusted setup without the risk of collision <dankrad> It's not so clear what a "collision" here means though. Really any version hash is only valuable if you know that DA was provided for it, and not on it's own. So the interesting property of the version hash is actually distinguishing different commitments *on the same* chain, and it isn't really necessary to provide different versions for other chains
